Accordion.name: Accordion
Accordion.role: A vertical stack of collapsible panels that shows and hides sections of content.
usage: Break long content into sections the reader expands on demand (FAQ, documentation)
Reveal details progressively without crowding the initial view
Group settings or options by category
Present questions and answers in a compact format
Walk through a hierarchy of content
constraints: **MUST NOT** — hold critical content that has to stay visible at all times
**MUST NOT** — nest an `Accordion` inside another: one level only
**MUST** — give each trigger explicit text, never an icon alone
**Note** — a disabled trigger drops pointer events and applies `opacity-disabled`
**MUST NOT** — serve as primary navigation → use `NavigationMenu` or `Tabs`

anatomy.role: A single panel, with a bottom border
Button that opens and closes the panel
Caret showing whether the panel is open
Panel content, animated as it opens

exports.name: Accordion
exports.description: The root of a stack of collapsible sections; set `type` to `single` or `multiple` to decide how many stay open.
exports.example:

  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionTrigger>Shipping</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Orders leave our warehouse within two days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

exports.name: AccordionItem
exports.description: One section of an `Accordion`, pairing a trigger with its content through a unique `value`.
exports.example:

    <AccordionTrigger>Returns</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>You can return any item within 30 days.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

exports.name: AccordionTrigger
exports.description: The text button that expands or collapses its `AccordionItem`; always give it a visible label, never an icon alone.
exports.example:

    <AccordionTrigger>How does billing work?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>You are billed on the first of each month.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

exports.description: The panel an `AccordionTrigger` reveals, holding the detail a reader opens on demand.

    <AccordionTrigger>Who can see my data?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Only the people you invite to your workspace.</AccordionContent>

Accordion.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Accordion](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/) (Radix Accordion)

**Role**: Each trigger is a `button` inside a heading, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; each panel is a `region` labeled by its trigger.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                     | Action                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space`       | Opens or closes the focused trigger's panel                                      |
| `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` | Next / previous trigger                                                          |
| `Home` / `End`          | First / last trigger                                                             |
| `Tab`                   | Moves to the next trigger, then past the accordion to the next focusable content |

**Accessible name**: The `AccordionTrigger` text names the button and labels the panel: it must describe the content, not say "See more".

**Pitfalls**:

- Do not put an interactive element inside `AccordionTrigger`: a button cannot contain another one.
- The heading level that wraps the trigger must fit the page's heading hierarchy.

Alert.name: Alert
Alert.role: A non-modal banner that delivers a contextual message — informational, a success, a warning or an error — with a title, a description and an optional action.
usage: Report an authentication error after a failed sign-in
Tell the user about a system state (session expired, network error)
Confirm an outcome the user should notice (payment sent, settings saved) → `variant="success"`
Warn about a risk the user can still act on (low balance, session about to expire) → `variant="warning"`
Warn before an irreversible action → `variant="warning"`; once the action has failed, `variant="destructive"`
Put an SVG icon first to strengthen the visual signal
constraints: **MUST NOT** — show a transient message (toast) → use `Sonner`
**MUST NOT** — act as a blocking dialog → use `AlertDialog`
**MUST NOT** — place more than one `Alert` per page section
**MUST NOT** — add a second `role="alert"` among the children: the root already carries it
**MUST NOT** — put variable-width content in `AlertAction`, which is absolutely positioned at the top right
dependencies: An SVG icon (Phosphor Icons) — a direct child of `Alert`, which switches the layout to two columns

Alert.accessibility:
**Pattern**: `alert` role (assertive live region)

**Role**: `role="alert"` on the root: screen readers announce the content as soon as it is inserted.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own; only the interactive elements placed inside receive focus.

**Accessible name**: The title (`AlertTitle`) and the description (`AlertDescription`) make up the announced message.

**Pitfalls**:

- `role="alert"` interrupts whatever is being read: keep `Alert` for important messages that appear in response to the user, not for a static notice present on page load.
- The `destructive`, `success` and `warning` variants do not carry the meaning on their own: the text must say what happened (icon plus words, never color alone). Success green and error red look alike to a red-green color-blind reader.
- **MUST NOT** — color an alert with a raw green or amber, or with `color.feedback.success.default` / `color.feedback.warning.default`: `text-success` and `text-warning` read the text tokens, which `tokens:lint-contrast` holds at 4.5:1 or more on the card in both modes.

divergences.note: A confirmed outcome the reader should notice (payment sent, settings saved): text-success on the card, with an icon. shadcn/ui has no success color, and the design system's Tailwind lockdown leaves no other conforming way to write one (color.md).

A risk the reader can still act on before it becomes an error (low balance, expiring session): text-warning on the card, with an icon. shadcn/ui has no warning color, and the Tailwind lockdown leaves no other conforming way to write one (color.md).

AlertDialog.name: AlertDialog
AlertDialog.role: A blocking modal that stops the user to confirm or cancel a critical action.
usage: Confirm an irreversible action (deletion, cancellation, final submission)
Ask for explicit approval before a destructive change
Show a warning the user has to answer
Block the rest of the interface until the user has made a choice

**Choice** (`rule-21`) — Pick the surface from how much it blocks and how long its content is. A blocking decision (confirm, destroy): `AlertDialog`. A short task with no inner scrolling: `Dialog`. Long content or side context: `Sheet` from `md` up, `Drawer` below — **unless** it is side navigation, which stays a `Sheet` at every width (this is what `Sidebar` does below `md`). Anchored, non-blocking content with no scrolling and at most 3 fields: `Popover`. An informative preview on hover, from `md` up: `HoverCard`. A one-line, non-interactive label of at most 80 characters: `Tooltip`.
constraints: **MUST NOT** — carry a plain informational message → use `Dialog`, or `Sonner` for a notification
**MUST NOT** — open an `AlertDialog` on top of another: one visible at a time
**MUST** — offer a cancel button (`AlertDialogCancel`)
**MUST NOT** — re-implement the focus trap: Radix provides it
**MUST** — render an `AlertDialogTitle`: it is the name screen readers announce
dependencies: `AlertDialog` from `radix-ui` (Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Title, Description, Action, Cancel)

anatomy.role: Portal that renders outside the parent DOM

AlertDialog.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Alert Dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/) (Radix AlertDialog)

**Role**: `role="alertdialog"`; labeled by `AlertDialogTitle`, described by `AlertDialogDescription`. Modal: while it is open, the rest of the page is `aria-hidden` (Radix sets no `aria-modal`).

**Keyboard**:

| Key                 | Action                                                      |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the focusable elements, trapped in the dialog |
| `Escape`            | Closes the dialog (same as Cancel)                          |
| `Enter` / `Space`   | Activates the focused button                                |

**Accessible name**: `AlertDialogTitle` is required; `AlertDialogDescription` must state what the action will do.

**Pitfalls**:

- On open, focus goes to `AlertDialogCancel`: the destructive action must never be the default choice.
- On close, focus returns to the trigger.
- Clicking outside does not close the dialog. That is deliberate: the decision must be explicit.
AlertDialog.code_example:
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/alert-dialog"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <AlertDialog>
      <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this item?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            This cannot be undone. The data will be permanently deleted.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Delete</AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  )
}

**MUST** — pass a single direct child; wrap several elements in a container

Attachment.name: Attachment
Attachment.role: A tile that stands for one file sent or received — its icon or preview, its name, its size — with its upload state and its actions.
usage: Show a file attached to a message, or queued in a composer before it is sent
Show the progress of an upload with `state="uploading"` or `state="processing"`, and a failed one with `state="error"`
Show an empty slot waiting for a file with `state="idle"` (dashed border)
Show an image preview with `AttachmentMedia variant="image"`, a file type icon with the default `variant="icon"`
Lay tiles out as a card with `orientation="vertical"`, or as a row (default)
Open the file on click with an `AttachmentTrigger` stretched over the tile
Remove or retry the file with `AttachmentAction` buttons in `AttachmentActions`
Scroll several tiles horizontally in an `AttachmentGroup`

**Choice** (`rule-23`) — Build a conversation from its family, one component per job. The scrolling thread that follows new messages: `MessageScroller`, one `MessageScrollerItem` per message. One turn of a speaker, with avatar, header and footer: `Message`, `align="end"` for the user's own turns. The text of a turn: `Bubble` inside `MessageContent`, `variant="ghost"` for an answer that reads as a document. An event nobody said (a date, a tool call, "Conversation resumed"): `Marker`, `variant="separator"` between days. A file sent or received: `Attachment`, several in an `AttachmentGroup`. Questions the assistant asks one at a time: `Questionnaire`; a form shown all at once, outside the thread: `Field`s in a `form`.
constraints: **MUST** — set `state` from the real upload: `uploading` while bytes are sent, `processing` while the server reads the file, `error` when it failed, `done` when it is usable
**MUST** — show the file name in `AttachmentTitle` and its size or type in `AttachmentDescription`; on `error`, say what failed in `AttachmentDescription`
**MUST** — give every `AttachmentAction` an `aria-label` that names the action and the file ("Remove report.pdf")
**MUST NOT** — put more than 2 `AttachmentAction`s in a tile → open a `DropdownMenu` from one of them
**MUST** — place `AttachmentTrigger` as the last child of the tile, with the file name as its accessible name, when the tile opens the file
**Note** — the `size` of `Attachment` takes `default`, `sm` and `xs`; the `size` of `AttachmentAction` takes the `Button` scale and defaults to `icon-xs`

**Note** — the tile orders its own parts with raw z-index values: `AttachmentTrigger` (`z-10`) lies over the media and the content, `AttachmentActions` (`z-20`) over the trigger. They are internal to the component, declared in `tokens/allow-raw.registry.json` (`local-stacking`) and listed in `specs/foundations/elevation.md`
dependencies: The `shimmer`, `scroll-fade-x` and `no-scrollbar` utilities of `shadcn/tailwind.css`, imported by `styles/globals.css`

Attachment.accessibility:
**Pattern**: A button (the trigger) and its secondary buttons (the actions), in a group

**Role**: `Attachment` is a `div` with no role. `AttachmentTrigger` is a native `button`, or a link through `asChild`. Each `AttachmentAction` is a `Button`.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                        | Action                                              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`                      | Moves to each action, then to the trigger           |
| `Enter`/`Space`            | Opens the file (trigger) or runs the action         |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Scrolls an `AttachmentGroup` horizontally, natively |

**Accessible name**: The trigger is stretched over the tile and holds no text: name it with `aria-label` (the file name, "Open report.pdf"). Each action is named by its `aria-label`.

**Pitfalls**:

- The upload state is shown by a shimmer and a color only: announce it in `AttachmentDescription` ("Uploading, 40%") or through a `role="status"` region.
- An image preview needs `alt` text; a type icon is decorative.
- The trigger covers the tile: an action outside `AttachmentActions` sits under it and cannot be clicked.

import {
  Attachment,
  AttachmentAction,
  AttachmentActions,
  AttachmentContent,
  AttachmentDescription,
  AttachmentGroup,
  AttachmentMedia,
  AttachmentTitle,
  AttachmentTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/attachment"
import { Spinner } from "@/components/ui/spinner"
import { FilePdfIcon, XIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <AttachmentGroup>
      <Attachment>
        <AttachmentMedia>
          <FilePdfIcon />
        </AttachmentMedia>
        <AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTitle>report.pdf</AttachmentTitle>
          <AttachmentDescription>2.4 MB</AttachmentDescription>
        </AttachmentContent>
        <AttachmentActions>
          <AttachmentAction aria-label="Remove report.pdf">
            <XIcon />
          </AttachmentAction>
        </AttachmentActions>
        <AttachmentTrigger aria-label="Open report.pdf" />
      </Attachment>
      <Attachment state="uploading">
        <AttachmentMedia>
          <Spinner />
        </AttachmentMedia>
        <AttachmentContent>
          <AttachmentTitle>photo.jpg</AttachmentTitle>
          <AttachmentDescription>Uploading, 40%</AttachmentDescription>
        </AttachmentContent>
      </Attachment>
    </AttachmentGroup>
  )
}

**Role**: No role: plain `div`s. `CardTitle` is not a heading element.

**Keyboard**:

No keyboard interaction of its own.

**Accessible name**: Not applicable. When the card is a section of the page, wrap its title in a heading of the right level (`Heading`).

**Pitfalls**:

- A fully clickable card must contain a real link (whose hit area can be stretched), not an `onClick` on the container.

Carousel.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Carousel](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/carousel/) (Embla)

**Role**: `role="region"` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; each slide is a `role="group"` with `aria-roledescription="slide"`.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                        | Action                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Previous / next slide, while focus is inside the carousel   |
| `Tab`                      | Reaches the previous / next buttons and the slides' content |

**Accessible name**: The previous / next buttons are named by `UI_STRINGS.carousel.previous` / `.next`. Give the carousel itself an `aria-label` ("Similar products").

**Pitfalls**:

- No auto-rotation without a pause button: content that moves on its own for more than 5 s must be stoppable (WCAG 2.2.2).
- The content of off-screen slides stays reachable from the keyboard: make sure the tab order still makes sense.

Chart.name: Chart
Chart.role: A container and a set of helpers for data visualization, built on `recharts`: theming, tooltips and a legend, all configured through a `ChartConfig` object.
usage: Draw bar, line, area or pie charts from structured data
Show a contextual tooltip when hovering a data point
Show a legend that describes the data series
Apply the theme's colors (light / dark) to the series automatically through `ChartConfig`
Wrap a `recharts` chart in a responsive container
constraints: **MUST NOT** — present raw data meant to be read value by value → use `Table`
**MUST** — pass `ChartContainer` a `config` with at least one entry
**Note** — in `ChartConfig`, `theme` takes precedence over `color`
**MUST** — read a series' color from the `--color-<key>` variable that `ChartStyle` injects for each `config` key (`fill="var(--color-revenue)"`); it is not a token: its value comes from `config`
**MUST NOT** — nest `ChartContainer`s: one container per chart

**MUST** — name the chart on the Recharts element, not on `ChartContainer`: `<BarChart accessibilityLayer aria-label="Revenue by month">`. The label reaches the focusable `<svg role="application">`; on `ChartContainer`, a `div` with no role, `aria-label` names nothing

**MUST** — give the chart a visible text summary of what it shows (its takeaway); give its data as a visible `Table` too when readers need the values, under a disclosure such as `Collapsible` if the screen is short on room
**MUST NOT** — hide a `Table` in `sr-only`: its scroll container then scrolls with nothing focusable in it (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`). Use a visible `Table`, or no table and the text summary
**MUST** — set `rootTabIndex={-1}` on a `<Pie>`: its layer is a second tab stop, and the chart surface already is one
**MUST NOT** — remove `ChartContainer`'s focus ring, or draw the focus of the chart another way: the container draws it while the chart has keyboard focus

Chart.accessibility:
**Pattern**: SVG chart (Recharts) — no APG pattern

**Role**: An SVG drawn by Recharts with its accessibility layer on (the default): the surface is a focusable `application`, named by the `aria-label` of the chart element. The tooltip appears on hover and, from the keyboard, on the data point the arrow keys reach.

**Keyboard**:

| Key                        | Action                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`        | Moves focus to the chart and away from it; `ChartContainer` shows its ring on every focus, with or without a `ChartTooltip` |
| `ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight` | Moves the tooltip and its cursor to the previous / next data point; the first one is shown when the chart receives focus    |
| `Enter`                    | Hides or shows the tooltip of the current data point                                                                        |

Everything the tooltip shows must also be in the text summary or the data table: a pointer user hovers, a keyboard user steps through the points, and neither is asked to find a value only the tooltip holds.

**Accessible name**: `aria-label` on the Recharts element (`BarChart`, `LineChart`, `PieChart`…) says what the chart shows; a visible title and a text summary of its takeaway sit next to it.

**Pitfalls**:

- Provide the data in another form as well (a visible text summary, a visible `Table`): a screen reader does not read bars. A chart with no `ChartTooltip` is still a tab stop where nothing changes but the ring; turn the layer off with `accessibilityLayer={false}` only when a table gives the same data.
- Categorical palette: the series stay distinct under color blindness (`npm run tokens:lint-chart`), but back the colors up with a legend or labels (see `specs/foundations/color.md`).

Checkbox.name: Checkbox
Checkbox.role: A two-state (or indeterminate) checkbox for selecting an option in a form, built on Radix `Checkbox.Root`.
usage: Accept terms of use or a privacy policy
Turn a preference on or off (for example "Remember me")
Select several entries in a list
Use the `indeterminate` state for a partially selected group: the box is filled and shows a minus

**Choice** (`rule-20`) — Pick the selection control from the number of options and the screen width. One value out of 2 to 5 options: `RadioGroup`, with every option visible. Out of 6 to 15: `Select` from `md` up; below `md`, `NativeSelect`, **unless** the options need rich rendering (icons, descriptions) → `Select`. More than 15 options, or search required: `Combobox`. Several values: `Checkbox` up to 5 options, `Combobox` in multiple mode beyond that. An on/off toggle that takes effect immediately: `Switch`.
constraints: **MUST** — pair the checkbox with a visible label: `Label` (`id` / `htmlFor`), or `Field` with a `FieldLabel`; inside a `Field` as soon as it has a description or an error message (`rule-09`)
**MUST NOT** — serve mutually exclusive choices → use `RadioGroup`
**MUST NOT** — let the enlarged hit area (`after:-inset-x-3 after:-inset-y-2`) overlap a neighboring control
**Note** — a disabled checkbox is not submitted with the native form
**MUST NOT** — convey a state through color alone: add an icon or text
dependencies: `CheckIcon` and `MinusIcon` from `@phosphor-icons/react` (sized `size-3.5`): the root's `data-state` shows `MinusIcon` when the box is indeterminate and `CheckIcon` otherwise
`Field` — required as soon as the checkbox has a description or an error message (`rule-09`)

anatomy.role: Radix `Checkbox.Indicator`, holds the `CheckIcon` and the `MinusIcon`, of which the root's `data-state` shows one

exports.description: A two-state or indeterminate choice in a form; pair it with a visible label and never use it for mutually exclusive options.

No dedicated style

`FOCUS_RING` (`lib/focus.ts`): `border-ring` border and a `ring-ring/50` ring `--space-focus-ring-width` wide. In a choice card (a `FieldLabel` that wraps a `Field`) the card draws the only ring: the box draws none and keeps its resting border. A box in a `FieldLabel` with no `Field` in it keeps its own ring
No dedicated style
`border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, `CheckIcon` visible
In a choice card, a focused unchecked box keeps `border-input`: the card draws the focus ring, not the box, and an invalid box keeps its `error` border. Elsewhere the resting look is `default`

`cursor-not-allowed` and `opacity-disabled`; a `Field` that holds a disabled `Checkbox` dims the box the same way (`group-has-[[data-slot=checkbox]:disabled]/field:opacity-disabled`); a disabled input next to an enabled box does not dim it

`aria-invalid="true"`: `border-destructive` (`border-destructive/50` in dark mode); on focus, a `ring-destructive/20` ring (`ring-destructive/40` in dark mode) and a solid `outline-destructive` outline `--border-width-default` wide; a checked or indeterminate box keeps `border-primary`, in light and dark mode

`checked="indeterminate"`: Radix sets `data-state="indeterminate"`, which fills the box like a checked one (`border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground`) and swaps the icon in CSS: the `MinusIcon` shows in place of the `CheckIcon`, and a click on an uncontrolled box shows the check again. At focus it takes `border-ring` like a checked box, and keeps `border-primary` in a choice card

Checkbox.accessibility:
**Pattern**: [Checkbox](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/) (Radix Checkbox)

**Role**: `role="checkbox"` on a `button`, with `aria-checked`: `true`, `false` or `mixed` (indeterminate).

**Keyboard**:

| Key     | Action                          |
| ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Space` | Checks / unchecks the box       |
| `Tab`   | Moves focus to the next element |

**Accessible name**: Required: a `Label` tied through `htmlFor` / `id`, or an `aria-label`. Clicking the label toggles the box.

**Pitfalls**:

- `Enter` does not toggle the box (native behavior): do not add it.
- `aria-invalid` styles the error; the message must be linked through `aria-describedby`.

Combobox.name: Combobox
Combobox.role: A text input with autocomplete that picks from a filterable list of options; supports single and multiple selection (chips).
usage: Pick a value from a long list (countries, cities)
Search and filter a data set as the user types
Select several values, shown as chips
Replace a native `<select>` when search is needed
Forms that benefit from assisted input (autocomplete)

**Choice** (`rule-20`) — Pick the selection control from the number of options and the screen width. One value out of 2 to 5 options: `RadioGroup`, with every option visible. Out of 6 to 15: `Select` from `md` up; below `md`, `NativeSelect`, **unless** the options need rich rendering (icons, descriptions) → `Select`. More than 15 options, or search required: `Combobox`. Several values: `Checkbox` up to 5 options, `Combobox` in multiple mode beyond that. An on/off toggle that takes effect immediately: `Switch`.
constraints: **MUST NOT** — be used for 15 options or fewer without search → `RadioGroup` up to 5, `Select` or `NativeSelect` from 6 to 15 (`rule-20`)
**MUST** — render a `ComboboxEmpty` for the "no results" case
**MUST** — in multiple selection, provide an `anchor` (`useComboboxAnchor`) so the popup opens below the chips
**MUST** — give each `ComboboxItem` a unique value
**MUST NOT** — receive a function (callback, event handler) from a server component: it is a client component (`"use client"`), and only serializable props reach it from a server component

**MUST** — in an interface that is not in English, translate the accessible names of the three icon-only buttons (trigger, clear, chip remove) through `triggerLabel`, `clearLabel` and `removeLabel`: they default to the English `UI_STRINGS.combobox`
**MUST** — pass `removeLabel` to a `ComboboxChip` whose children are not the item's text: the default name is built from the chip's rendered text, so each remove button says which item it removes
dependencies: `@base-ui/react` — the `Combobox` primitive (Root, Value, Trigger, Clear, Input, Popup, Positioner, Portal, List, Item, ItemIndicator, Group, GroupLabel, Collection, Empty, Separator, Chips, Chip, ChipRemove)

- The content must stay visible while the pointer is over the tooltip itself (WCAG 1.4.13): do not shorten the delays.

import {
  Tooltip,
  TooltipContent,
  TooltipProvider,
  TooltipTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/tooltip"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Kbd } from "@/components/ui/kbd"
import { CopyIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger asChild>
          <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Copy">
            <CopyIcon />
          </Button>
        </TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent>
          Copy <Kbd>⌘C</Kbd>
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  )
}
